SOURCE DATA:
- DemoBottling-Shift-Log-2026-09-17-Day.csv (entries at 10:42, 10:50, 11:05, 11:40) – TIER 2 EVENT
- FL‑101‑SOP.txt (Revision 1.0) – Sections 6.1, 6.2, 6.3, 6.4, 12.3, 13 – TIER 2 DOCUMENT
- FL‑101‑Work‑Instruction.txt – WI‑FL101‑001 – TIER 2 DOCUMENT
- Knowledge Graph entry for FL‑101 – Glass Breakage fault, criticality, procedures – TIER 1 VERIFIED

WHAT IS THE ISSUE:
- Broken glass observed on the floor beside the filler; no glass alarm was triggered and the line is still running.
- SOP and knowledge‑graph classify any glass breakage as a CRITICAL product‑safety event requiring immediate line stop, LOTO, QA hold, and cleanup.
- This occurrence differs from the only prior recorded glass‑break alarm (2026‑09‑17) where the alarm stopped the line automatically; the current event escaped detection.

WHAT IS THE IMPACT:
- Production impact: line must be stopped for safe cleanup; current operation poses risk of contaminating product.
- Safety risk: CRITICAL – broken glass can enter filled bottles and cause injury or product recall.
- Financial impact: potential loss of product from QA hold (all bottles filled in the last 30 min) and downtime for cleanup and sanitation.

HOW CRITICAL IS IT:
- CRITICAL – SOP explicitly states broken glass is a product‑safety event (GBP‑001) and mandates immediate shutdown, LOTO, and QA hold.

HOW TO ADDRESS IT:
- Immediate action:
  Step 1: Safety — Activate the emergency stop, then perform LOTO according to SAF‑003 (switch off main isolator, apply personal lock, tag with name/date, verify lockout).
  Step 2: Diagnosis — Visually confirm location of broken glass; ensure no bottles are open within 2 m of the break.
  Step 3: Fix — Place every bottle filled in the last 30 min on QA HOLD and label; discard any open bottles within 2 m; clean broken glass using the red glass kit and a vacuum only (no compressed air).
  Step 4: Verify — Perform the mandatory 10‑minute sanitation rinse of the filler (bowl, valves, nozzles) as per WI‑FL101‑001 Step 9.
  Step 5: Quality — Obtain sign‑off from the quality lead before restarting; record the incident in the glass‑breakage log.
- Root cause fix (permanent solution):
  - Inspect and calibrate the glass‑breakage detection sensor to ensure future alarms trigger; replace faulty sensor if needed.
- Preventive action:
  - Add a daily pre‑start visual inspection of the star wheel and filler interior for glass fragments.
  - Conduct quarterly functional tests of the glass‑breakage alarm system.
  - Reinforce operator training on immediate stop and LOTO when any glass is observed.
- Who to notify:
  - Quality Lead
  - Maintenance Supervisor
  - Shift Supervisor

PLANT MANAGER SUMMARY

SITUATION: Broken glass was found on the floor of Filling Line 1 with no alarm, but the line is still running.  
ROOT CAUSE: Glass breakage occurred; the detection alarm failed to trigger, creating a product‑safety risk.  
STATUS: Line must be stopped, cleaned, and sanitized before restart.  
ACTION REQUIRED: Stop the line, apply LOTO, place recent bottles on QA HOLD, clean the glass with the red kit, perform the mandatory sanitation rinse, and obtain quality‑lead sign‑off.  
RISK IF NOT ACTIONED: Contaminated product could reach customers, leading to injury, recall, and severe financial loss.

2. SCOPE

Applies to all 24 fill valves on the FL-101 Bottle Filler. Only trained
maintenance technicians may carry out this work.

3. WHEN TO REPLACE THE SEALS

Replace the seal kit when:
  - A valve drips between fills
  - The checkweigher shows the same valve underfilling again and again
  - Three or more underfill alarms happen in one shift
  - The seal has reached its limit: 3 months or 1,500 running hours,
    whichever comes first

4. TIME NEEDED

  One valve:                     about 15 minutes
  A typical job (1 to 4 valves): 30 to 45 minutes
  Including rinse and check:     about 1 hour

5. PARTS AND TOOLS

  Seal kit, one per valve:  SEAL-FV-24 (main seal and O-ring)
  Food-grade lubricant:     FGL-1
  Location:                 Filling Line 1 spares cabinet, shelf 2
  Tools:                    valve key, seal pick, clean lint-free cloths,
                            20 empty 500 ml bottles for the check

6. SAFETY

---

6.1 PPE required on Filling Line 1
  - Safety glasses at all times
  - Cut-resistant gloves when handling glass or change parts
  - Hearing protection
  - Safety shoes

6.2 Lockout / tagout (LOTO)
LOTO is required before any maintenance, clearing a jam, changing parts, or
reaching into the machine. Follow SAF-003:
  1. Switch off power at the main isolator.
  2. Lock the isolator with your personal padlock.
  3. Tag it with your name and the date.
  4. Try to start the machine to prove it cannot run.
Only the person who fitted a lock may remove it.

6.3 Guards
All guard doors have safety switches. The machine stops if a guard door is
opened. Never bypass or tape over a guard switch.

6.4 Main safety rules
  - Never clear a jam while the machine is running.
  - Never reach past a guard.
  - Never use compressed air near open bottles or broken glass.
  - Keep the floor dry. Report leaks and spills straight away.

If a bottle breaks during a jam, stop and follow Section 12.3.

12.3 Glass Breakage
Alarm message: "Glass breakage detected in filler"

CRITICAL — broken glass can end up inside filled bottles. This is a
product safety event. Follow GBP-001.

Immediate action:
  Step 1 — Stop the line at once with the emergency stop.
  Step 2 — Do not open any guard until the machine has stopped and is
           locked out (Section 6.2).
  Step 3 — Put every bottle filled in the last 30 minutes on hold. Label
           them QA HOLD. Throw away any open bottles within 2 metres of
           the break.
  Step 4 — Clean up with the red glass kit only. Use a vacuum, never
           compressed air (air spreads glass).
  Step 5 — Rinse the filler (sanitation rinse, 10 minutes).
  Step 6 — The quality lead must sign off before the line restarts.
  Step 7 — Record the event in the glass breakage log.

Bottles on QA HOLD may only be released after the quality lead has
inspected them.
